why: The project's 300 MW IT load assumes an N+1 configuration of 121 diesel generators at 2,500 kW each, yielding a computed NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy under the assumptions of 500 hours per year operation and 6.4 g/kWh NOx (Tier 2 diesel). This NOx potential to emit exceeds the 100 tpy major-source threshold under 40 CFR 70.2, triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. The 300 MW load also exceeds the 75 MW threshold in Texas SB 6, invoking large-load interconnection standards that require additional ERCOT studies and financial assurances. Furthermore, the Governor's directive mandates that the PUCT and ERCOT complete a data center interconnection audit before any data center project moves forward, creating a prerequisite for this 300 MW project. While no local moratorium or county opposition is indicated for this incorporated Abilene site, the combined federal air permitting, state large-load interconnection rules, and mandatory audit create significant regulatory conditions that must be satisfied before the project can proceed.

needs_confirmation.text: The why-chain link from 300 MW IT load to 1,067 tpy NOx potential to emit relies on unverified assumptions (N+1 diesel generators, 2,500 kW each, 500 h/yr, 6.4 g/kWh NOx Tier 2). These assumptions are not supported by a verified quote; only the 100 tpy threshold is verified. A plausible alternative (e.g., natural gas generators with ~0.5 g/kWh NOx) would reduce NOx to ~83 tpy, below the major-source threshold, flipping the finding.

The audit may apply to all data centers regardless of size, making the 75 MW threshold a misreading.
